turns.prompt_text: what's the difference between hemp and marijuana
turns.response_html:
The primary difference between hemp and marijuana is their THC content and legal classification, even though they both belong to the Cannabis sativa L. plant species.

Key Differences

  • THC Levels: Hemp is legally defined as cannabis containing 0.3% or less THC by dry weight. Marijuana contains significantly higher levels, typically ranging from 5% to 30% or more, which produces a psychoactive "high."
  • Usage: Hemp is a versatile industrial crop used for textiles, paper, biofuel, and CBD extraction. Marijuana is primarily cultivated for medical or recreational use due to its intoxicating effects.
  • Legal Status: Under the 2018 Farm Bill, hemp is federally legal in the United States. Marijuana remains a Schedule I controlled substance under federal law, though many states have legalized it individually.
  • Cultivation: Hemp is grown closely together to encourage tall stalks and seed production. Marijuana is usually spaced out to encourage the growth of resinous flowers (buds) on female plants.
